observation_summary: FastDateFormat caches instances using a key that incorrectly excludes the locale when it is null, causing the cache to return stale instances when the default locale changes.
reasoning_summary: The bug is in the caching logic (the algorithm for generating the cache key). The original implementation conditionally added the locale to the key only if it was non-null, which meant that if the locale was null, the cache key did not reflect the current default locale. When the default locale changed, the cache returned an object created with the old default locale. The fix modifies the algorithm to ensure the locale is always part of the cache key, correctly using the default locale if the provided one is null. This is a procedural correction to the caching strategy.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'The FastDateFormat getDateInstance() and getDateTimeInstance() methods create the HashMap key from various items including the locale. If the locale is null, then it is not made part of the key... If the Locale is changed subsequently, then the wrong locale is applied.'

The fix diff shows the removal of the conditional 'if (locale != null)' check for key creation and replaces it with an unconditional inclusion of the locale in the key, ensuring the cache key is always locale-aware.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves assigning a value to 'locale' if it is null, the core issue is the logic of the cache key generation algorithm, not just an incorrect initialization.
The fix involves changing the logic of how the key is constructed, not just adding a missing guard or validation check.
